title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din lived 1137-1193 in Egypt/Syria and never set foot in Iberia; the in-game text even calls the foe 'Saladin's Emir', compounding the error. AoE2 offers alternatives (e.g. a generic Sultan/King unit, a renamed Castle-unit hero) so this was entirely avoidable.

28 CAMEL_RIDER for the Muslim side: Andalusi taifa and even Almoravid forces in Iberia fought as light javelin cavalry (jinetes), Berber infantry and heavy horse; massed camelry is North African/Levantine, not peninsular. Light Cavalry/Knights/Skirmishers were available in the engine.
31 CAVALRY_ARCHER as the enemy core: horse-archery was not a characteristic Andalusi/Almoravid arm; this is a steppe/Turkic template.

KING units in both Player Two and Player Three rosters represent nobody in the historical situation (al-Mutamin is voiced in text but never placed as a distinct figure), and give a European monarch model to Muslim taifa rulers.

A single monolithic 'Almoravid emir' enemy for the whole 1081-1094 span: the Almoravids only crossed to Iberia in 1086 and El Cid's Zaragoza-era opponents were Christian (Aragon, Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona) as often as Muslim; none of those belligerents appear at all.
